runs.name: bc_accounts
runs.text: How would Brand Concierge answer our customers' questions about accounts and rates?

sections: Our approach
We would deliver this with Brand Concierge.
What we would do

We will set up the Brand Concierge experience for the agreed banking or insurance products: connect and curate the approved content sources, design the conversations and guardrails for the agreed questions, configure the brand voice and the required disclosures, set up the handoff (live chat, meeting booking or both) routed to your designated team, build, with your reviewers, the golden-answer test set (including the priority discovery questions from the Brand Visibility program) and the refusal and escalation scenarios, complete Adobe's pre-go-live checks, and launch on the agreed pages in stages.

runs.name: bv_chatgpt
runs.text: Describe how Brand Visibility shows where our brand appears in ChatGPT answers.

lines: L02: Brand Visibility setup and baseline [one-time]
L01: Prompt strategy and measurement plan [one-time]
O01: Monthly prompt and performance review [monthly]
O02: Content improvements for search and AI [monthly]
sections: Our approach
We would deliver this with Brand Visibility.
What we would do

We will configure the agreed monitoring portfolio (200 to 1,000 prompts in up to three markets or languages), validate access for up to 10 pilot users, confirm the delivery-network setup and register CDN log forwarding in Brand Visibility and confirm the logs arrive once the log-forwarding job is active in your CDN console, and record one baseline for the agreed prompts and three competitors.
We will run two discovery workshops and curate 200 to 1,000 prompts in up to three markets or languages, covering agreed customer intents, three competitors and five business measures.
After launch

We will maintain the prompt portfolio (200 to 1,000 prompts in up to three markets or languages) and three competitors; review up to five prompt changes, read the Impact Measurement Engine's results when Adobe generates an analysis for an eligible deployment pilot, prioritize up to 10 actions, and hold one review with you using five business measures.

We will refresh four existing pages and create one new answer/knowledge page using approved facts and existing templates, in one locale with two review rounds. Each page change is logged once and tagged search, AI or both.

runs.name: assets_cif
runs.text: How would approved AEM Assets images reach Adobe Commerce product pages through the CIF add-on?

lines: XC15: Migrate Commerce media to AEM Assets [one-time]
XC13: Set up AEM Assets for Commerce metadata [one-time]
XC14: Connect Commerce and set SKU matching [one-time]
AS01: DAM onboarding, users and access [one-time]
sections: Our approach

The AEM Assets Integration for Commerce links approved AEM Assets to Commerce products by SKU, or by custom matching built in Adobe Developer App Builder, and syncs them into the catalog; merchandisers can also pick DAM assets inside the Commerce Admin. On Commerce on Cloud and on-premises it's an Adobe extension we install; on Commerce as a Cloud Service it's configured in the Commerce Admin.
Merchandisers manage product images once in AEM Assets; approved images tagged with SKUs reach Commerce products, most within five minutes, keeping storefronts accurate and on brand.
What we would do

We will move existing product media from Commerce into AEM Assets, map product SKUs, image roles and positions, and approve the assets. Migrate category media separately and agree how it will be reassigned. Keep Commerce as Visualization Owner until product synchronization completes.
We will enable the Commerce integration in Cloud Manager (or install the assets-commerce package on older releases), activate Dynamic Media with OpenAPI, and set the approval metadata schema.
We will set IMS permissions and the AEM Assets Integration settings in the Commerce Admin, choose Match by product SKU, set the Visualization Owner and start the first sync.
We will add users to the Admin Console, create user groups and attach the AEM Assets product profiles, and confirm the Cloud Manager program and environments for the DAM.

runs.name: commerce_aem
runs.text: How does Adobe Commerce connect to AEM Sites?

lines: XC10: Connect AEM Sites to Commerce with CIF [one-time]
SI02: Site build with components and templates [one-time]
sections: Our approach

The Commerce Integration Framework (CIF) add-on, provisioned by Adobe, connects AEM Sites as a Cloud Service to the Adobe Commerce GraphQL endpoint so authors can search, browse and use product data in AEM. It suits headless AEM content and existing CIF sites: the CIF storefront and CIF Core Components are in maintenance mode, and Adobe recommends Edge Delivery with the Commerce Storefront for new storefronts, while documenting a headless AEM storefront that starts with the CIF add-on.
Authors find real products from the Commerce catalog while building headless content, and pages on existing CIF sites, so shopping content uses live product data instead of copied details.
What we would do
We will once Adobe provisions the CIF add-on, set the COMMERCE_ENDPOINT variable for each environment in Cloud Manager and the CIF configuration for store view and catalog root.

We will build the commerce-specific content (product teasers, category and campaign content, Content Fragments) that authors assemble from products they search and browse in AEM, using Content Fragments and headless content for new builds rather than CIF Core Components.
We will build the site from the AEM Project Archetype or a Site Template, with Core Components, editable templates, client-side libraries and the custom components the design needs.
